newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to scrap royalty paid by refineries.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to scrap royalty paid by refineries.

text.p: Thailand's National Energy Policy Office (NEPO) will soon ask the cabinet to scrap a two percent royalty on oil sales, a senior official said on Thursday.
The move is in line with an attempt to provide equal treatment of local refineries and a policy of deregulating the energy industry.
NEPO policy and planning analyst Suwaporn Sirikoon told Reuters the agency made the decision on Monday to abolish the royalty calculated from sales of oil refineries.
The decision came after some oil refineries complained that they paid a higher royalty than competitors in other countries, Suwaporn said.
NEPO also decided at the meeting that it would propose to the cabinet to raise the fuel oil excise tax to 1.5 satangs per litre from 1.0 satang, she said.
"NEPO's decision is expected to be submitted to the cabinet for its approval later this month," Suwaporn said.
